description: WHEN LOW-VALUES of the ordered EVALUATE CONFIRMI at app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:173-191 - the arm at :183, which shares a single body with WHEN SPACES at :182, that body being PERFORM READ-ACCTDAT-FILE at :184. SERVICE. THE PAIRED COUNTERPART OF case10, AND THE PAIR IS THE POINT. COBOL lets consecutive WHEN clauses stack onto one body, and this EVALUATE alone uses the idiom three times - 'Y' at :174 with 'y' at :175, 'N' at :178 with 'n' at :179, and SPACES at :182 with LOW-VALUES at :183 - with a fourth at :533 where DFHRESP(DUPKEY) and DFHRESP(DUPREC) stack. A stacked clause is only genuinely covered by a case that matches THAT clause. case10 arrives with a blank CONFIRMI and matches :182; this case arrives with a byte of X'00' and matches :183; neither can reach the other's clause, and one case for the pair would leave half the idiom asserted by nothing while the case count still read twenty. The outcome the two reach is deliberately identical - read the account, then ask the user to confirm - because that is what makes the pair a test of the DISPATCH rather than of the body. IN SOURCE ORDER, AND THE ORDER IS THE BEHAVIOUR. :156 SET CONF-PAY-NO TO TRUE, before any validation, so CONF-PAY-YES is false for the whole invocation and that one statement is why :210 takes its ELSE. :158-167 EVALUATE TRUE finds ACTIDINI non-blank and takes WHEN OTHER / CONTINUE at :165-166 - a genuine no-op arm, and no error. :169 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON opens, and :170-171 is one MOVE with two receivers, ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI to ACCT-ID and to XREF-ACCT-ID, PIC X(11) into two PIC 9(11) items, with NO NUMERIC VALIDATION ANYWHERE IN THE PROGRAM. None is added here (practice B5): the identifier seeded is eleven digits, so the move is unremarkable, and inventing an edit the source does not perform would be a different program. :173-191 then evaluates CONFIRMI in exact source order - WHEN 'Y' at :174 and WHEN 'y' at :175 do not match, WHEN 'N' at :178 and WHEN 'n' at :179 do not match, WHEN SPACES at :182 does NOT match because the byte is X'00' and not a blank, WHEN LOW-VALUES at :183 MATCHES, and WHEN OTHER at :185 is never reached. EVALUATE takes the first matching WHEN and WHEN OTHER is the default, so an implementation that reordered the arms, merged the two into one test, or let one fall through into the next would be a different program (gate G30). Note what this arm does NOT do: unlike :176-177 it does not SET CONF-PAY-YES, and that omission is the whole distinction between a lookup and a payment. ONE BYTE, NOT ELEVEN. CONFIRMI is PIC X(1) at app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:72, so LOW-VALUES here is a SINGLE X'00' - contrast case09, whose subject is ACTIDINI at PIC X(11) and whose eleven X'00' bytes reach the :159 SPACES OR LOW-VALUES test through its LOW-VALUES disjunct. The JSON representation is the one case09 settled and is reused unchanged so the corpus carries one convention and not two: the six-character JSON escape for U+0000 in the case text, which survives a parse round trip as a NUL character, rather than a literal NUL byte in the file. A single X'00' is not a single space, and the distinction is load-bearing rather than pedantic - had the byte arrived as a blank, this case would have matched :182, duplicated case10 exactly, asserted that clause twice and the LOW-VALUES clause never. The byte is echoed back in CONFIRMO and compared there, so FieldDiffer tells the two apart instead of conflating them. A DIFFERENT FIXTURE ROW FROM case10's, SO A SECOND BALANCE IS DECODED (gate G16). case03, case10 and case15 all seed row 0; this case seeds ROW 29 of the fifty in src/test/resources/fixtures/acctdata.txt, which is byte-identical to the real app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt - 15,050 bytes, 50 rows of exactly 300. That row is ACCT-ID 00000000030 and its raw twelve-byte ACCT-CURR-BAL field is 00000000020{, THE SMALLEST POSITIVE BALANCE IN THE CORPUS at 2.00, the fifty ranging from 2.00 up to 843.00. It was chosen for that property and not for convenience: :198 tests IF ACCT-CURR-BAL <= ZEROS, and 2.00 is the closest the real data comes to that boundary, which makes this the sharpest available evidence that the comparison is against zero rather than against one and that no rounding to whole dollars has crept into the decode. The row was chosen, never edited - not one byte under app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms or app/data was modified to make a value here convenient (practice B3). THE 300-BYTE RECORD, SUMMED FROM app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy RATHER THAN FROM PROSE (practice B11). ACCT-ID 9(11) at 1-11, ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 12, ACCT-CURR-BAL S9(10)V99 at 13-24, ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT at 25-36, ACCT-CASH-CREDIT-LIMIT at 37-48, ACCT-OPEN-DATE X(10) at 49-58, the misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) at 59-68, ACCT-REISSUE-DATE X(10) at 69-78, ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT at 79-90, ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT at 91-102, ACCT-ADDR-ZIP X(10) at 103-112, ACCT-GROUP-ID X(10) at 113-122 and FILLER X(178) at 123-300. That is 300, the RECLN the copybook's own header states and the width every one of the fifty fixture rows occupies (gate G19). For this row the thirteen spans are 00000000030, Y, 00000000020{, 00000001200{ for the 120.00 credit limit, 00000000930{ for the 93.00 cash limit, 2011-08-26, 2024-06-27, 2024-06-27, 00000000000{ and 00000000000{ for the two 0.00 cycle amounts, A000000000, ten spaces, and 178 spaces. ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE IS MISSPELLED IN THE COPYBOOK AT CVACT01Y.cpy:11 AND IS MISSPELLED HERE (requirement I1): correcting it to ACCT-EXPIRATION-DATE would leave the diff looking for a span the decoder never produces, which is a silent parity break rather than a loud one. FILLER X(178) IS PINNED, AS 178 SPACES (gate G21) - it is an addressable span and not a gap, and omitting it would make the image 122 bytes and shift every offset after it, which is why the complete 300-byte image is pinned alongside the thirteen named fields. THE OFFSET TRAP, VERIFIED BY SLICING THIS ROW RATHER THAN BY READING PROSE ABOUT IT: offsets 103-112 hold A000000000 and that span is ACCT-ADDR-ZIP, while ACCT-GROUP-ID at 113-122 holds TEN SPACES. Prose elsewhere describes A000000000 as a group-id trailer; it is not, and a case that believed it would pin two fields wrongly while the total width still summed to 300. ZONED DECIMAL, TRUNCATION, AND WHY THE BYTES ARE PINNED AND NOT THE QUANTITY. S9(10)V99 occupies exactly twelve character positions - ten integer digits and two fraction digits - and the sign consumes no position of its own, which is the only reading under which the copybook sums to 300. The sign is overpunched into the TRAILING byte, and in all fifty fixture rows that byte is '{', a positive sign carrying a low-order digit of zero. So the stored image 00000000020{ carries the digits 000000000200, whose first ten are the integer part 0000000002 and whose last two are the fraction 00: the value is 2.00, not 20.00. The five monetary spans are therefore expected AS THEIR STORED TWELVE-BYTE IMAGES, transcribed from the fixture, because pinning the image rather than a decimal literal pins the OVERPUNCH BYTE ITSELF - the unsigned form 000000000200 decodes to the same quantity but is not what COBOL writes into a signed DISPLAY item, and a byte-level gate exists to report that difference. Where the quantity is modelled in Java it is a BigDecimal at SCALE 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN and never a double or a float (AAP rules R2 and R4, gate G23): a V-scale scan of all 28 copybooks returns only V99, and the keyword ROUNDED appears zero times in all 28 programs, so truncation toward zero is the only faithful mode - never HALF_UP and never HALF_EVEN. No arithmetic runs on this path, so nothing here needs a rounding decision; the mode is named because the DECODE of a stored span is where a wrong scale would first show, and because 2.00 is the row where a scale error would look most plausible. THERE IS NO COMP-3 IN ANY COPYBOOK IN THIS REPOSITORY - verified zero - so no packed-decimal nibble unpacking is involved; the WS-ABS-TIME PIC S9(15) COMP-3 at COBIL00C.cbl:59 is working storage and is never persisted. THE READ IS ISSUED WITH UPDATE, ON A PATH THAT WRITES NOTHING. :184 performs READ-ACCTDAT-FILE, which at :345-354 is EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-ACCTDAT-FILE) INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) LENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCOUNT-RECORD) RIDFLD(ACCT-ID) KEYLENGTH(LENGTH OF ACCT-ID) UPDATE RESP(WS-RESP-CD) RESP2(WS-REAS-CD), and the EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :356-372 takes its first arm, WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :357, whose body is CONTINUE. In Java that is AccountRepository.readForUpdate and the record is HELD (gate G47, the read-for-update NORMAL arm). Nothing is rewritten afterwards and no ENDBR or release is issued - the lock is simply left to the end of the task. That is the source behaviour and it is preserved, not corrected (practice B5). WS-ACCTDAT-FILE is 'ACCTDAT ' at :41, the CICS FILE name the online programs use; the dataset is addressed here by the binding key ACCTDAT that src/main/resources/application-test.yml declares for it, never by a literal dataset name. THE EDITED BALANCE IS A DIFFERENT FIELD FROM THE STORED ONE, AT A DIFFERENT WIDTH. :193 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO WS-CURR-BAL and :194 MOVE WS-CURR-BAL TO CURBALI OF COBIL0AI sit INSIDE the :169 guard but OUTSIDE the EVALUATE, so they run on every stage-two arm including the ones that have already sent a screen. WS-CURR-BAL is PIC +9999999999.99 at :56 - a sign position, ten integer positions, an actual decimal point character and two fraction positions, which is fourteen bytes and an exact fit for the symbolic map's CURBALI PIC X(14) at app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:66. For 2.00 it renders +0000000002.00: a leading plus because the value is at or above zero, then NINE LEADING ZEROS AND A 2, because the picture is +9999999999.99 and not +ZZZZZZZZZ9.99 - there is no zero suppression and no thousands separator anywhere in it. That is why the smallest balance in the corpus is the useful one to render: a formatter that suppressed leading zeros, or that emitted 2.00 or +2.00, would differ from COBOL on this row by eleven characters and could not hide. Do not confuse these fourteen edited characters with the twelve zoned bytes of the record span; they are two representations of one quantity and both are pinned, at their own widths. STAGE THREE PASSES AND STAGE FOUR PROMPTS. :197-206 tests IF ACCT-CURR-BAL <= ZEROS AND ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES - a conjunction, and the balance just read is 2.00, which is above zero, so the 'You have nothing to pay...' rejection does not fire and no error flag is raised. :208 opens the last guard, :210 IF CONF-PAY-YES is FALSE because :156 set CONF-PAY-NO and :183-184 never changed it, so control reaches the ELSE at :236: :237-238 MOVE 'Confirm to make a bill payment...' TO WS-MESSAGE and :239 MOVE -1 TO CONFIRML OF COBIL0AI. The -1 is CURSOR METADATA and not payload - CONFIRML is the xxxL length item, which is how COBOL positions the cursor - so it is declared as cursorField rather than as a screen field. Note what is ABSENT from this arm: it sets NO error flag. It is a prompt asking the user to type Y or N, not a rejection, and that difference is exactly why :242 PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN is reached. ONE SEND, AND ITS FOUR FIELDS. :242 is the only send on this path, so the expectation carries exactly one. SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN at :289-301 performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :291, moves the eighty-byte WS-MESSAGE over the seventy-eight-byte ERRMSGO at :293 - the two-byte loss is the picture difference between PIC X(80) and PIC X(78) and not a shortened expectation - and then issues EXEC CICS SEND MAP('COBIL0A') MAPSET('COBIL00') FROM(COBIL0AO) ERASE CURSOR at :295-301. ERRMSGO is therefore the 33-character message left-justified and space-padded to exactly 78. ACTIDINO is the eleven characters as received, CURBALO the fourteen just edited, and CONFIRMO the single X'00' that arrived - unchanged, because no statement on this arm writes it, and INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :560, the only paragraph that blanks it, is reached only from CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN at :554 - itself performed at :137 and from the 'N' arm at :180 - and from the transaction-WRITE success arm at :524, none of which this path takes. The four are addressed as xxxO items because app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:79 declares COBIL0AO REDEFINES COBIL0AI, so the input and the output views are ONE SPAN: a value received in CONFIRMI is observable in CONFIRMO, and :298 sends FROM(COBIL0AO). THE HEADER SIX ARE THE CONTROLLER'S AND ARE DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED HERE. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :319-338 writes TRNNAME 'CB00', PGMNAME 'COBIL00C', TITLE01 and TITLE02 as app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 declares them at their full PIC X(40) width - '      AWS Mainframe Modernization       ' with six leading and seven trailing blanks and '              CardDemo                  ' with fourteen leading and eighteen trailing - and CURDATE and CURTIME as the eight-byte MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS groups of app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, which at this case's pinned instant are 07/19/22 and 23:12:32. Those six carry no decision and are projected by BillPaymentController, not by the service under test here, so a SERVICE case that declared them would be claiming fields its own unit does not write. They are asserted where they belong: case01 and case03 pin all ten items of the map. WHAT DOES NOT HAPPEN, AND WHY THAT IS AN ASSERTION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. Everything between :211 and :235 is inside IF CONF-PAY-YES and none of it runs: READ-CXACAIX-FILE, MOVE HIGH-VALUES TO TRAN-ID, STARTBR / READPREV / ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE, the INITIALIZE and the eleven moves that assemble the 350-byte transaction, GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP, WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE, the program's single COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT at :234, and UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE at :235. So expectedWrites is EMPTY, which is the positive assertion that nothing was written anywhere - not an absence of interest - and expectedFinalState pins the seeded account row byte for byte to prove the record is still there, unchanged, after a read that held it for update. The dataset-level expectations say the rest: ACCTDAT holds zero rows on the WRITES channel and one on FINAL_STATE, and TRANSACT holds zero on both. Those two zero counts are the only way to state 'the transaction master was reported and produced nothing', because a channel with no row has no row for a row-level expectation to address; each also pins the width that identifies the dataset, 300 for CVACT01Y and 350 for CVTRA05Y. ONLY ACCTDAT IS SEEDED, AND NO LINE IS EMITTED. The cross-reference is read by READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :408-436, performed only at :211 inside the unreached payment block, so seeding CXACAIX would assert a read this arm does not make, and normalisations is empty as a consequence - the recorded cardxref 36-to-50 filler pad has nothing to apply to, and a normalisation naming a dataset the case does not seed cannot fire. expectedMessages is empty because every DISPLAY in the program - :366, :397, :430, :461, :490 and :541 - sits in a WHEN OTHER arm of a file operation, and this path takes the NORMAL arm of the only file operation it performs. The confirmation prompt is SCREEN TEXT, not an emitted line: it is asserted once, as ERRMSGO on the send that produced it, and declaring it a second time on a message channel would claim an emission the program never made. The attribute map is empty and must stay empty: COBIL00C's COPY list at :63-85 is COCOM01Y, COBIL00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVACT01Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - NEITHER CSSETATY NOR CSSTRPFY IS COPIED and DFHRED appears nowhere in the program's 572 lines - so there is no red-and-asterisk highlight to expect, and the one attribute byte the program ever writes is the DFHGREEN of :526, on the transaction-WRITE success arm this path never reaches. STATELESSNESS, AND THE CONTEXT STAYS 1. EIBCALEN is 218: the 160 bytes app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy declares for CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 58 bytes of the CDEMO-CB00-INFO group COBIL00C.cbl:64-72 appends inside the same 01 group. The area arrives with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT of 1, which is what :112 tests through CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and is the REENTER half of gate G38, and it leaves as 1: no XCTL occurs on this arm, so RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN and its MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT at :280 are never reached and the next invocation re-enters again. All sixteen shared spans travel back exactly as they arrived, because no statement on this path writes one - CDEMO-ACCT-ID stays eleven zeros even though an account was just read, which is the source behaviour and not an oversight. All of it - the area, the AID and the screen values - travels in the payload, so no server-side session state exists or is implied (gate G37, AAP rule R6). DETERMINISM. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant the program's own version footer at :571 carries, and it is the SAME instant every other case in this directory pins; the header date and time are derived from that injected Clock through common/DateHeader and never from a captured now (practice B7). Two-digit month, day and hour, no midnight and no daylight-saving edge, so neither rendering is ambiguous. NO 26-BYTE TIMESTAMP IS PRODUCED ON THIS PATH: GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP is performed only at :230, inside the unreached payment block, so nothing here composes TRAN-ORIG-TS or TRAN-PROC-TS. US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, which for a nine-fixture ASCII corpus and a twelve-dataset EBCDIC one is the difference between a comparison and a coincidence (practice B8). UNIT KIND. SERVICE, driving BillPaymentService.processEnterKey - the real @Service, constructed through its own constructor and called as a plain object, with NO HTTP, no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no application context anywhere in the path (gate G51). That is where the decision logic of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY lives, which is exactly why the service split exists and exactly why a parity case must reach it with nothing in between; the unit of work is real, because :351 states the UPDATE option and a record lock outside a unit of work is released before the task that asked for it can rely on it. PROVENANCE. Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - read out of app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:173-191, :193-194, :236-242 and :343-372, cross-checked against the byte layout of app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COBIL00.bms, the X(40) VALUE literals of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, the 160-byte layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, the CB00 transaction and ACCTDAT file definitions of app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD, and row 29 of the real app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, whose raw twelve-byte ACCT-CURR-BAL field is 00000000020{ and which is byte-identical to the shipped src/test/resources/fixtures/acctdata.txt - and it WAS NOT CAPTURED FROM A LIVE COBOL EXECUTION, not one byte of it. Such a capture is empirically impossible in this environment: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - both copied by this program at :84-85 - absent from the repository, which is why the DFHENTER mnemonic this case declares comes from common/CicsAid, the single reproduction of DFHAID, rather than from a copybook. AAP 0.7.6 documents eight verified blockers, 0.9.11 records the substitution as risk R-A escalated for confirmation rather than absorbed, and 0.9.12 records the missing copybooks as risk R-D. GATES. G15 (one of the twenty cases of this program), G16 (seeded from the real acctdata.txt, at a row case10 does not use), G18 (the diff count must be zero), G19 (the 300-byte width), G21 (FILLER emitted and space-filled), G23 (scale 2), G30 (EVALUATE CONFIRMI order preserved, SPACES and LOW-VALUES as two distinct stacked clauses, WHEN OTHER last), G37 (no server-side state), G38 (the REENTER side), G47 (the READ-ACCTDAT-FILE NORMAL arm) and G51 (reached without HTTP or a JobLauncher). NOT APPLICABLE HERE, AND NOT INVENTED: the CSSETATY DFHRED-and-asterisk highlight, since neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY is copied and DFHRED never appears; G24 and G28, since the single COMPUTE at :234 is not reached; G45, since the CXACAIX finder is not reached; G32, since the program contains no GO TO; G35, since it contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and never touches RETURN-CODE, which is why the expected return code is 0; G39, since this screen has no pagination; and G40, since no XCTL occurs. No user rules were provided for this project - review_rules returns exactly one line saying so - so no rule governs this file; the enterprise practices B1, B3, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 stand in their place and are honoured above.
